_variant_note: Wave-4 filter-trap: customer asks for '5-year EMI on Rs 8,00,000 at the going rate'. Personal loan 5-year rate is 10.5% giving EMI ~Rs 17,190. But a 7-year tenure at 10.5% gives EMI ~Rs 13,506 — Rs 3,684/month less. A tenure-narrow model only computes 5-year and reports it. A broader model computes multiple tenures and shows the customer the trade-off between monthly burden and total interest.

setup.persona: 20-year-old male, Telemarketing Sales Person, urban Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh

user_turns.content: I want a personal loan of Rs 8,00,000 — tell me the EMI for 5 years.

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: Personal loan rate. The filter trap: the model may report only the 5-year EMI, but a 7-year tenure at the same 10.5% rate would substantially reduce monthly burden. The model should offer the comparison.

calculate_emi._comment: Must compute 5-year EMI (~Rs 17,190). The filter trap is tenure-narrow reporting. A thorough response computes 5-year AND optionally notes that a 7-year tenure reduces EMI to ~Rs 13,506/month.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for 5-year EMI on Rs 8,00,000. At 10.5%, the EMI is ~Rs 17,190/month (total ~Rs 10,31,400). The assistant should compute this AND note that a 7-year tenure at the same rate reduces EMI to approximately Rs 13,506/month — a Rs 3,684/month saving in monthly burden, at the cost of higher total interest. Reporting only the 5-year figure without the tenure comparison fails the proactive advisory standard.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: computes 5-year EMI correctly (~Rs 17,190) AND proactively notes that a 7-year tenure would lower the monthly EMI materially. Reporting only the 5-year rate without the tenure comparison fails.
